- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.8) and forecast is high, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid over-optimism.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.5) and forecast is low, increase forecast by 5–10% to avoid underestimating downside.  
- After a sharp price spike, model tends to overcorrect — reduce forecast by 10–15% in the next 3–5 days to allow for mean reversion.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (±0.3 to 0.7) and forecast deviates >5% from true, apply a smoothing filter: average last 3 true values before adjusting.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the period — adjust downward by 2–5% for days 1–7 if sentiment is weak or mixed.  
- If sentiment shows increasing negativity over 3–5 days, model tends to lag — forecast should be adjusted upward by 3–7% to account for sentiment-driven reversal.
